mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 anticipates higher future discount rates on corporate cash flows, leading to negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the identified FEDFUNDS rise, with a p-value > 0.05 in a backtest.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 jobs over two consecutive months is associated with stronger consumer demand, pushing S&P 500 forward returns to the positive over a 60-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >=50,000 over two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified labor expansion phase.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDPC1 (GDP) and HOUST (retail sales) show double-digit growth in the prior quarter, the S&P 500 expects a near-term demand-driven rally, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows >10% and HOUST grows >10% in the previous quarter
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative or flat despite the combined growth signal, with a p-value > 0.05 in a rolling window test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 5% or more, followed by a rebound of at least 3% in the next month, predicts a supply-side adjustment that precedes S&P 500 bearishness over a 5-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >5% in month t, then rises >=3% in month t+1
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified supply adjustment pattern.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS above 3%, the S&P 500 expects negative 20-day forward returns as higher policy rates compress equity discounting.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive or flat during the high-rate regime, with a p-value > 0.05 in a regime-sliced backtest.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% followed by a sustained rise above 4.5% creates expectations of tighter labor markets, pushing S&P 500 forward returns to the positive over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for a month, then UNRATE > 4.5% for the next 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative during the identified labor tightening phase, with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) exceeding 2% growth in the prior quarter triggers a demand dual signal that drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 2% and RSAFS > 2% in the previous quarter
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite the dual growth signal in a controlled out-of-sample test.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month streak of monthly industrial production declines of 2% or more predicts a supply-side pessimism that results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >=2% each month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the two-month contraction period.
